A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EDDP research. Their complete main texts and appendices support comparison of methods, equations, experiments, tables, and figures despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments, evaluations on deep image classifiers, ablations, and a watermark-based model-correction experiment, with additional empirical results in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and appendix results, and additionally reports intermediate outcomes in the counterfactual example.

M1.justification: Equation (13) removes the previously listed, otherwise undefined L_cs ≤ tau_cs constraint. This is a limited correction to the stated optimization problem; the estimator, losses otherwise defined, UFM/CFM procedures, and four-stage learning process remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the synthetic study, Broden/Broden-Action concept data, ImageNet/Places365/Moments-in-Time evaluations, and clean/poisoned Chess Pieces experiments. No dataset, domain, or task coverage is added.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain PCA, NMF, Natural, IBD, Pattern-CAVs, and the appendix UIBE/CBE comparisons. v2 clarifies how its PCA/NMF implementations differ from cited methods without establishing a change in evaluated comparator membership.

E3.justification: The architectures, splits, cluster counts, metrics, training schedules, and testing procedures are retained. Newly specified NMF parameters document the existing experiment, while the counterfactual intermediate steps were already described in v1.

E4.justification: Section 7.10 adds intermediate-stage evidence showing the effect of concept removal before concept addition in the counterfactual case study. The existing loss ablations, margin sensitivity studies, faithfulness assessments, and other case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across concept detectors and retain the same RCAV permutation tests, Bonferroni correction, and ten random-direction trials in the model-correction example. No new repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Section 7.10 newly reports confidence of 30.5% after road removal and 70.4% after building removal, with neither removal changing the predicted class. The completed replacements retain their 22% and 57% confidence values, and the benchmark and ablation table results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 removes the explicit F ≤ D − I restriction on the distractor-basis dimension. The feature-manipulation and concept-contribution derivations are retained, largely relocated to Appendices A.4–A.6 rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: v1's broad framing of comparisons against the previous unsupervised state of the art is narrowed to the evaluated baselines. v2 explicitly distinguishes these baselines from complete prior implementations in Section 7.5; the central EDDP and application contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 7.5 and Appendix A.12 explain why class-conditioned prior methods are not directly comparable with this class-agnostic evaluation. They newly acknowledge that omitting NMF recursivity and PCA gradient re-ranking may make the evaluated baselines less effective, qualifying interpretation of the retained results.

D1.justification: v2 adds Algorithm 1, including running-statistics guidance, specifies NMF beta = 2 and tolerance 1e−6, and reports GPU configurations and architecture-specific runtimes in Appendix A.21. Most other implementation and training details are retained or relocated.

R1.justification: v2 adds Anders et al. (2020), Neuhaus et al. (2023), and Gao et al. (2025), and removes Fel et al.'s paper on magnitude-constrained feature visualization. It also refines its positioning relative to class-conditioned PCA/NMF approaches; the remaining Fel citation-letter changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method overview undergo substantial rewriting and condensation. Detailed application derivations and experimental settings move into organized appendix sections, while the main text replaces lengthy derivations with explanatory summaries.

P2.justification: v2 adds the loss-summary Table 1 and an algorithm display, revises captions, and relocates existing plots, including v1 Figures 27–28 becoming v2 Figures 23–24. Existing visual content and table structures are largely retained, although many images have lower resolution.

improvement.justification: v2 improves readability, documents implementation and computing requirements more clearly, and better qualifies what the baseline comparisons establish. These are useful but limited gains because the principal empirical evidence is unchanged. Lower-resolution figures modestly reduce visual detail, but do not outweigh the improvements in clarity and transparency.
